text:
Alyssa (Support): Hey team, AcmeCorp reporting intermittent SSL/TLS handshake failures (502/SSL_error) for their private VPC after last night's scheduled cert rotation at ~02:00 UTC. ~30% of requests fail, other hosts in same VPC succeed. Customer says errors started immediately after rotation.

rotator-bot: Rotation completed for tenant=acmecorp at 2026-02-18T02:00:05Z (new leaf + intermediate uploaded).

Alyssa (Support): I asked them for reproducer but they attached a short curl trace and a backend app log. Attaching here:
```
curl -v https://api.internal.acme.svc:443/health --resolve api.internal.acme.svc:443:10.10.5.12
*   Trying 10.10.5.12:443... connected
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
```

Alyssa (Support): They also ran openssl s_client from inside their VPC and attached cert chain (shows only leaf + single intermediate).

Jordan (Eng): Can we get a copy of the cert bundle the rotator served during that rotation? Also need tcpdump from their side showing handshake, and a dig +short for the hostname in their kube nodes (split-horizon?).

Mike L (SRE): Quick checks: 1) Are we serving fullchain on the internal LB? 2) Any AIA fetching differences — some clients do path building by fetching missing intermediates. If our internal network blocks AIA egress, that can break clients that rely on AIA.

Alyssa (Support): Customer confirms they block outbound HTTP/80 from nodes by default. They said external tests (from public internet) succeed. This hints internal clients cannot fetch missing intermediate via AIA.

Jordan (Eng): Ok suspicion: rotator uploaded cross-signed intermediate to the public bundle, but our internal LB config (haproxy/nginx) might be serving an alternate chain due to split-horizon cert store (we have a feature that symlinks internal bundles during private deploy). If internal bundle lacks the cross-signed intermediate, internal clients that do path-building and that expect cross-sign may fail.

Mike L (SRE): Ask customer to run these quick checks and paste outputs:
```
# show served cert chain from inside VPC
openssl s_client -connect api.internal.acme.svc:443 -showcerts -servername api.internal.acme.svc </dev/null | sed -n '1,120p'
# DNS resolution from pod/node
dig +short api.internal.acme.svc
# curl with verbose + ssl verify
curl -v --cacert /path/to/customer/truststore https://api.internal.acme.svc/ -k
```

Customer: AcmeCorp: pasted outputs — s_client shows two cert blocks (leaf + intermediate-sans-only). Public verification we ran externally shows leaf + intermediate + cross-signed intermediate. We also saw our nodes return the internal VIP 10.10.5.12 consistently.

Jordan (Eng): That matches split-horizon mismatch. The rotator likely uploaded a bundle containing both intermediates, but the internal bundle used by the private LB was rebuilt from the tenant-specific internal store which only had the new intermediate (not the cross-signed one). Our internal path->chain selection then served the shorter chain. Because the customer blocks AIA egress, their clients couldn't fetch the missing cross-signed issuer, failing path building.

Alyssa (Support): Is this the same as a "misordered bundle" or different root cause? I want a one-line to tell the customer so they can scope remediation.

Jordan (Eng): One-line: "Internal LB served an incomplete intermediate chain due to a split-horizon internal bundle missing the cross-signed intermediate; internal clients cannot fetch missing issuers because outbound HTTP for AIA is blocked."

Alyssa (Support): Customer asked for immediate workaround while we fix rotator. Any quick customer-side fix?

Mike L (SRE): Workarounds: 1) Add the cross-signed intermediate to their node truststore (or fullchain file) so path building succeeds locally. 2) Temporarily allow outbound HTTP/80 from nodes to the AIA URL (least effort). 3) Configure clients to use the fullchain we provide (bundle pinned).

Jordan (Eng): I'll patch rotator to ensure internal bundle generation copies the fullchain (prefer cross-signed intermediate first), and add a validation step that simulates blocked AIA (validate that chain is self-contained). Adding a unit test for private deployments.

rotator-bot: New hotfix branch created: rotator/private-bundle-include-cross-issuer, PR #847.

Jordan (Eng): Deploy plan: 1) push hotfix to build pipeline, 2) roll to staging private tenant replicas, 3) health check, 4) schedule hotfix rollout to affected tenant (acmecorp) with a canary. Should be low-risk but needs owner's ok.

Alyssa (Support): Customer prefers we push the fix; they can accept a brief maintenance window. They asked if any config they should change on their side to avoid recurrence.

Jordan (Eng): Recommend: 1) Use fullchain in app (do not rely on AIA fetching). 2) If they must block outbound HTTP, keep the cross-signed intermediates in their node truststore. 3) Monitor for any upcoming rotations where we will push validation warnings.

Alyssa (Support): Sent plan to customer with estimated ETA: hotfix rollout tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. Requested tcpdump after hotfix if they still see failures.

Customer: AcmeCorp: thanks, will schedule maintenance and report back. :+1:

Mike L (SRE): After rollout, I validated on staging that internal LB served fullchain (shows leaf + intermediate + cross-signed intermediate) and curl from simulated blocked node succeeded. Putting a post-rotation test into CI to detect internal-only missing intermediates.

Alyssa (Support): Filing follow-up doc with remediation steps and checklist for private deploys. Closing thread once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
